content:
Looking at each piece, I need to check whether two congruent copies can be joined end-to-end to trace a simple closed curve.

- **A, C, D:** These spiral/hook shapes, when paired with any congruent copy (rotated 180° or reflected) so that endpoints meet, force overlapping segments or self-intersections — the inner "hook" always collides with the copy.
- **B:** The zigzag wave has collinear middle segments; any copy matched end-to-end makes the flat portions overlap instead of enclosing a region.
- **E:** Taking the piece and its 180° rotation about the midpoint of its endpoints aligns the U-shaped part with the tail part perfectly, enclosing a region with no crossings — the ends meet exactly and the union is a simple closed polygon.

Thus the piece that works is E.

\boxed{E}
